findings.message: `completeReached` picks its open releases with a plain select (line 86). It then locks each one with `tracked()`, but never checks the status again after the lock. If a concurrent `record_deployment` completes the release between the select and the lock, `completeBy` still runs on the completed row. `writeStatus` then overwrites `completed_at`, `completed_day`, `completed_zone`, `completion` and `completing_deployment_id`. Because the status is unchanged, it writes no history row, so the overwrite is silent. This breaks 126's rule that Completed is final. The fix: after `tracked()`, skip any row whose `r.status === 'completed'`. Or select the open releases `for update` with the `status <> 'completed'` predicate, so READ COMMITTED checks it again under the lock. Add a two-session race test (record_deployment to the current Prod environment against upsert_environment making the reached QA environment Prod).
findings.scenario: p1 is category prod, with a live QA deployment at T1. Session A runs upsert_environment {name: QA, isProd: true}: it takes the project lock, updates the environments and selects p1 as open. Session B runs record_deployment p1 → Prod (the old Prod; A's change isn't committed yet). B locks p1 and completes it on the Prod deployment at T2, Late, then commits. A's `tracked(p1)` gets the lock and reads status completed. `reachedAlready` finds the QA record at T1, and `completeBy` rewrites p1 to completed at T1, On time, `completing_deployment_id` = the QA record. No history row is written, and the Prod deployment that actually completed it is no longer marked.

findings.message: An environment upsert can now complete releases, but its audit row only records the environment: `after: input`, resourceId = the environment. Nothing in the audit says which releases it completed or on which deployment. The module standard says every write is audited. Here, release rows are changed by a service whose audit doesn't mention them, and their history rows say `source: deployment`, which hides that an environment change caused the completion. Fix: return the completed releases (version and completing deployment id) from `completeReached` and put them in the upsert's audit `after` (e.g. `after: { ...input, completed: [...] }`). Assert them in the existing QA-made-Prod test.
findings.scenario: p1 (prod) has a live QA deployment. upsert_environment {name: QA, isProd: true} completes p1. The audit trail has only `delivery.environment.upsert` with {name: QA, isProd: true}. Nothing audited names p1 or says the environment change completed it, and p1's status history reads `completed:deployment` as if a deployment had done it.

findings.message: `upsertEnvironment` now completes releases (it writes status, completed_at, completed_day, completion and completing_deployment_id on `delivery.release`), but the service's audit row only covers the environment: `resourceId` is the environment's id and `after` is the raw input. Nothing in the audit names the releases this call completed. The status-history row says `source: 'deployment'`, which hides that an environment change caused the completion. `updateRelease` puts the new status in its audited `after`. Fix: return the ids and versions of the completed releases from `completeReached` and include them in the upsert's audited `after` (for example `after: { ...input, completed: [...] }`). Use a history source or reason that shows an environment change caused the completion.
findings.scenario: An Admin marks QA as Prod and open release p1 (already deployed to QA) completes. The audit event for delivery.environment shows only {projectKey, name:'QA', isProd:true}. No audit record anywhere says p1 changed, and its history row reads 'completed by deployment, by Admin'.
